title: Genetic Screening for Women Seeking Fertility Treatment
what_it_is: Genetic Screening for Women Seeking Fertility Treatment

sections.label: Pre-implantation Genetic Screening review
sections.summary: MOH is reviewing PGS clinical effectiveness and ethics, with NUH running a three-year pilot programme starting by early next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MOH had previously received requests to allow Pre-implantation Genetic Screening (PGS) to identify chromosomal abnormalities in embryos created through in-vitro fertilisation (IVF), with the aim of improving the chances of conceiving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We had not granted approval so far as the published evidence had been unclear.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In recent years, however, newer technologies for PGS have emerged and some jurisdictions have now allowed PGS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MOH is, therefore, reviewing the clinical effectiveness of PGS and its ethical implications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To assess clinical effectiveness, NUH will be conducting a three-year pilot PGS programme which will commence by early next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MOH will also look into the ethical concerns and regulation of PGS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For example, we will need to ensure that embryos are not eliminated solely based on parental preferences on characteristics, such as gender.
